name: Bladder Cancer
remarks: Urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder: incidence, presentation,
TURBT and pathology, risk-stratified non-muscle-invasive management,
muscle-invasive and metastatic treatment, surveillance, and end of life.
INCIDENCE. Annual reroll from age 45 (Guard), on an age-banded,
sex-specific schedule carrying a 2x multiplier for EVER-smokers
(ever-smokers keep the drawn hazard, never-smokers half of it). Male
4.1e-03 (75+); female one quarter of the corresponding male value.
That is ~1.78x the SEER 22 (2017-2021) male age-specific rates of
the cohort the population-average multiplier is 0.684, so the realised
population-average rate is ~1.22x SEER. Integrated over the realised
ages of a 400-patient run's 346 males that expects 7.34 diagnoses
(2.12% of males) against 6.08 (1.76%) for a SEER-exact schedule.
Pre-fix the module rolled a flat unconditional hazard every year from
infancy (0.25%/yr for a quarter of men, 0.08%/yr for the rest),
producing a measured 23.5% male prevalence in the same 400-patient run
and onsets in children.
Sources: SEER*Explorer, urinary bladder, SEER 22 2017-2021 age-specific
incidence and DevCan lifetime risk (~3.9%, 1 in 26, for US males);
Freedman ND et al., JAMA 2011;306:737 (smoking attributable risk);
Cumberbatch MGK et al., Eur Urol 2018;74:784.
ENCOUNTER ARCHITECTURE. Every clinical state -- ConditionOnset,
Procedure, MedicationOrder, Observation -- fires inside an open
encounter, and every encounter is explicitly closed before any Delay of
a day or more. The three pre-fix encounter locks (Medical_Oncology
~13-16 weeks, Intravesical ~10 weeks, Hospice 30-180 days on every death
path) are gone: intravesical therapy is now six weekly closed
instillation visits, chemotherapy is per-cycle closed infusion visits,
and hospice is a same-day enrolment encounter followed by repeating
closed 14-30 day benefit periods. The `*_Supply_Delay` idiom (a 30-day
Delay standing in for a pharmacy fill, inside an open encounter) has
been removed entirely; infusional and intravesical agents are ordered
with `administration: true` so they bill as J-codes on carrier and
outpatient claims instead of as Part D fills, and the two oral
antiemetics are ordered and explicitly ended after a three-day course.
RECURRENCE AND PROGRESSION are per-pass hazards derived from the EORTC
risk tables (Sylvester RJ et al., Eur Urol 2006;49:466) rather than the
pre-fix flat 15%/pass recurrence and 5%/pass progression.
CODING. Fifteen SNOMED codes were wrong and have been replaced against
the SNOMED CT international edition; see the individual state remarks.
Two failed the SNOMED Verhoeff check outright ("122985900", a dropped
check digit for 1229859000 pT3 (AJCC); "369974005", not a concept).
Palliative_Care_Consultation no longer uses 103735009, which other
modules use as a CarePlanStart and which therefore silently discarded
whole patient records through a ClassCastException in
HealthRecord.careplanStart.
Bladder cancer before 45 is vanishingly rare (SEER age-specific rates
under 45 are < 2 per 100,000 person-years, and under 20 essentially
zero). The pre-fix module rolled an unconditional annual hazard from
infancy, which is why it produced onsets in children and a ~25%
male lifetime risk.
One incidence roll per year of life from age 45.
Age-banded, sex-specific annual hazard. The values are the EVER-SMOKER
hazard: Smoking_Risk_Filter passes every ever-smoker but only half of
the never-smokers, so the realised ever-smoker:never-smoker ratio is
exactly 2:1 and the never-smoker hazard is half of each value here.
SEER 22 (2017-2021) male age-specific urinary-bladder incidence, for
side-by-side comparison, runs about:
so the drawn schedule is ~1.78x SEER at every band. Ever-smokers are
36.8% of this simulated cohort (measured from the tobacco-status
observations of a 400-patient run), which makes the population-average
multiplier 0.368*1.0 + 0.632*0.5 = 0.684, and the population-average
realised rate therefore 1.78 * 0.684 = ~1.22x SEER. Integrated over the
realised ages of that run's 346 males the schedule expects 7.34
diagnoses (2.12% of males) against 6.08 (1.76%) for a SEER-exact
schedule. The ~4:1 male:female weighting matches the SEER incidence
ratio of ~3.5:1.
Branch order matters: ComplexTransition takes the FIRST true branch, so
the oldest band is tested first within each sex, and the male branches
precede the unconditioned female defaults.
EVER-smoker test, not current-smoker. Testing `smoker == true`
alone is a trap: LifecycleModule.startSmoking assigns the stock
`smoker` attribute once at age 16, but LifecycleModule.quitSmoking
then clears it back to false with probability 0.01 per 7-day
timestep (the quit probability is clamped at the 0.01 baseline, so
it never decays), which leaves P(still flagged `smoker` at age 45)
= 0.99^(52*29) ~ 2.6e-07. Measured on a 400-patient run, the
tobacco-status observations recorded at age 45 or over contain
18637 `Never smoked tobacco` and 12770 `Ex-smoker` and ZERO
`Smokes tobacco daily`. A current-smoker test therefore selects
nobody at the ages this module cares about.
`quit smoking age` is set by quitSmoking at the moment a smoker
quits, so (smoker == true) OR (quit smoking age is not nil) is the
ever-smoker set: 266/723 = 36.8% of that cohort. This is the same
idiom lung_cancer/lung_cancer_probabilities.json uses.
Tobacco is the dominant modifiable risk factor for urothelial
carcinoma -- current smokers ~3x and former smokers ~2x the risk
of never-smokers, ~50% of US cases attributable (Freedman ND et
al., JAMA 2011;306:737; Cumberbatch MGK et al., Eur Urol
2018;74:784). A pooled 2x for ever-smokers is applied here.
Utilities.compare returns false for a null lhs and handles
`is not nil` before the null check, so both legs are null-safe.
Never-smokers keep half of the drawn hazard, so the drawn value
is the ever-smoker rate and half of it is the never-smoker rate.
Biological onset. No record entry is written here -- the patient
is not yet diagnosed. The umbrella diagnosis is recorded at the
pathology review visit (Develop_Bladder_Cancer).
Painless gross haematuria is the presenting symptom in ~80-90%
of bladder cancers; irritative voiding symptoms dominate in CIS.
Almost every patient with gross haematuria is referred; a
minority are managed expectantly first.

remarks: Specimen turnaround happens between visits, not inside one.
Every diagnostic ConditionOnset in this module fires inside an
open encounter. Pre-fix, the site and stage onsets fired after
TURBT_Encounter_End with nothing open, so they were silently
attributed to whatever stale encounter had the latest start.

remarks: The umbrella diagnosis. Pre-fix this state was unreachable -- no
transition anywhere in the module pointed at it -- so no patient
ever carried a non-site-specific bladder-cancer code. It now fires
once, at the pathology review visit, on every diagnosed patient,
immediately after the site-specific onset, and supplies the
encounter `reason` for every subsequent visit.
~75% of incident bladder cancers are non-muscle-invasive (Ta/T1/CIS)
and ~25% muscle-invasive or beyond at presentation.

codes.display: Carcinoma in situ of urinary bladder

remarks: Pre-fix this was a single ConditionOnset carrying SNOMED
"122985900" -- 1229859000 pT3 (AJCC) with its Verhoeff check
digit dropped, and therefore not a SNOMED code at all. Split into
the two real stages it was trying to represent.
Intermediate-risk Ta disease: single immediate post-TURBT
instillation of mitomycin C in most patients.

codes.display: Administration of chemotherapeutic agent into urinary bladder via intravesical route

remarks: Six weekly intravesical instillations, each its own closed
outpatient visit. Pre-fix, one ambulatory encounter was opened
and held across a 30-day `_Supply_Delay` plus a 6-week
'induction cycles' Delay -- ~10 weeks of encounter lock per
patient, during which no wellness or urgent-care visit could
be scheduled for that person by any module.

codes.display: Administration into urinary bladder via intravesical route

remarks: SWOG 8507 maintenance: 3 weekly instillations repeated at
roughly 6-month intervals (Lamm DL et al., J Urol
2000;163:1124). Three maintenance courses (~1.5 years) are
modelled; each instillation is its own closed visit.

codes.display: Administration into urinary bladder via intravesical route

remarks: Recurrence/progression detected at the between-course cystoscopy;
the onsets fire inside this open visit.
Per-pass (not per-year) hazards, with the surveillance interval of
3-6 months (mean 4.5) folded in, stratified by the EORTC/EAU risk
group recorded at diagnosis:
low  (Ta low grade)  : 5.5% recurrence, 0.30% progression per pass
intermediate (Ta HG) : 8.5% recurrence, 1.0% progression per pass
high (T1 HG / CIS)   : 11.5% recurrence, 2.5% progression per pass
That is ~8%/6 months recurrence for low risk (1-year ~15%, 5-year ~55%)
and 0.8%/yr progression for Ta low grade (5-year ~4%), versus ~20-30%
5-year progression for T1 high grade / CIS.
Sources: Sylvester RJ et al., Eur Urol 2006;49:466 (EORTC risk tables);
Cambier S et al., Eur Urol 2016;69:60 (EORTC BCG-maintenance tables);
EAU NMIBC guideline 2023.
Pre-fix these were flat 15% recurrence and 5% progression PER PASS,
i.e. ~40%/yr and ~12%/yr, so essentially every Ta low-grade patient
progressed to muscle-invasive disease within a few years.
Pre-fix this carried SNOMED 405843009, which is "Widespread
metastatic malignant neoplastic disease" and is mapped by
condition_code_map to ICD-10 C54.1 (recurrent endometrial
carcinoma) -- so every NMIBC recurrence in this module billed as
an endometrial cancer. 263855007 is the code the module already
used for its other recurrences and maps to C67.9.
Pre-fix 369974005, which fails the SNOMED Verhoeff check and is
not a SNOMED concept.

codes.display: Cystoscopy and transurethral resection of neoplasm of urinary bladder

remarks: Intravesical gemcitabine for BCG-recurrent NMIBC: six weekly
instillations (Addeo R et al., J Clin Oncol 2010;28:543).

codes.display: Administration of chemotherapeutic agent into urinary bladder via intravesical route

remarks: Pre-fix the 30% who did not proceed to cystectomy went straight
to Palliative_Care_Referral and then hospice death, i.e. a third
of BCG-unresponsive NON-muscle-invasive patients died of their
cancer inside a year. They now continue bladder-sparing
surveillance, which is what actually happens.

CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis

remarks: Pre-fix 261004008, which is "Diagnostic intent" -- a qualifier
value, not a disorder.
Shared closer for both staging encounters -- EncounterEnd closes
whichever encounter is currently open.
Neoadjuvant cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy before
radical cystectomy gives a ~5% absolute 5-year survival
benefit (Advanced Bladder Cancer Meta-analysis Collaboration,
Eur Urol 2005;48:202). Gemcitabine + cisplatin q21d x 4 is
the standard schedule.
Pre-fix, Medical_Oncology_Encounter opened one ambulatory
encounter, ordered cisplatin, then held the lock across a
30-day `_Supply_Delay` and a 9-12 week 'cycles' Delay --
~13-16 weeks of encounter starvation, and every subsequent
chemotherapy order in the module ran with nothing open.
Oral antiemetic, a real dispensed prescription (Part D), so it is
ordered without `administration` and explicitly ended three days
later. HealthRecord.medicationStart is idempotent while a drug is
present, so without the MedicationEnd the first cycle's order would
stay open forever and later cycles would be silent no-ops.

legitimately sit inside an open encounter, and only for an
inpatient/SNF/hospice class.
Pre-fix 182840001, which is "Drug treatment stopped - medical
advice" -- the engine's own MedicationEnd reason code.
Pre-fix 261004008 "Diagnostic intent".

as six weekly closed visits, each delivering a radiotherapy
fraction plus radiosensitising cisplatin (James ND et al.,
First-line gemcitabine + cisplatin, up to 6 q21d cycles
(von der Maase H et al., J Clin Oncol 2005;23:4602).

remarks: Pre-fix this used LOINC 58410-2 (a CBC panel code) with no value at
all. Renal function is what is actually monitored after urinary
diversion.

codes.display: CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis

remarks: 3% per 3-6 month pass compounds to ~35% recurrence at 5 years,
which is the observed figure after radical cystectomy
(Stein JP et al., J Clin Oncol 2001;19:666). Pre-fix it was 12%
per pass, i.e. ~82% at 5 years.
Recurrence after cystectomy is systemic disease and is treated on
the metastatic pathway.
~28% intravesical recurrence at 5 years after trimodal therapy
(Mak RH et al., J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3801). Pre-fix 20% per pass
made bladder preservation fail in ~94% of patients by 5 years.

codes.display: Cystoscopy and transurethral resection of neoplasm of urinary bladder

remarks: Disease-free long-term survivor.
Pre-fix, long-term survivorship was a bare annual Delay loop that
generated no encounter at all -- survivors vanished from the
claims record entirely between events.
The annual survivorship loop can run for decades, so the
second-primary onset is guarded to fire at most once per
patient.
Second primary malignancy after bladder cancer (most often lung or
upper-tract urothelial); ~1%/yr excess is consistent with SEER
multiple-primary data. Pre-fix this fired at 3%/yr, unguarded.
A small share of long-term survivors leave this module's care
pathway entirely (cured, or transferred out).
Pre-fix the progression ConditionOnset fired with no encounter open.
Pre-fix, Palliative_Care_Referral was a bare Procedure with no
encounter open that transitioned straight into Hospice_Enrollment,
so every palliative referral in the module was in fact an
immediate hospice enrolment followed by death within 30-180 days.
The module's own Palliative_Phase / Palliative_Radiotherapy /
Comfort_Care_Only subgraph was unreachable.
CODE COLLISION FIX. Pre-fix this Procedure carried SNOMED
103735009 "Palliative care", which six other modules
(prostate_cancer, dlbcl, ovarian_cancer, pancreatic_cancer,
myelodysplastic_syndromes, small_cell_lung_cancer) use as a
CarePlanStart. HealthRecord.present is keyed by code and stores
heterogeneous Entry subclasses, so a patient who acquired the
Procedure and then hit any CarePlanStart with the same code
threw ClassCastException in HealthRecord.careplanStart and was
DROPPED FROM THE EXPORT ENTIRELY. 713281006 "Consultation for
palliative care" is the correct concept for a palliative-care
referral consult and is used nowhere else in the module tree.
A 5-fraction palliative haemostatic course for tumour bleeding.
Comfort-care follow-up is bounded: after at most six visits
(~9 months) the patient transitions to hospice.
Pre-fix this was an AMBULATORY encounter held open across a
30-180 day Hospice_Period Delay, on every death path in the
module. That single reservation blocked wellness and urgent-care
scheduling for the patient's entire final six months.
Enrolment is a same-day encounter and is closed immediately.
Repeating hospice benefit periods, each opened and explicitly
closed. A bounded 14-30 day stay inside a hospice-class
encounter is a genuine length of stay, not a lock.
